title: Why phones die faster in the cold

idea.hook_angle: Your battery isn't broken, it's frozen
idea.why_trending: First cold snap of the season; people are posting 40%-to-0% screenshots.

script.title: Why Your Phone Dies in the Cold
script.hook: Your phone isn't dying. It's freezing.
scenes: Lithium ions move through a liquid inside your battery.
Cold makes that liquid sluggish, so the ions crawl.
Your phone sees low voltage and panics, shutting down early.
Warm it in your pocket and most of that charge comes back.
script.description: Why your battery percentage plummets in the cold, and how to get it back.

idea.hook_angle: 30 minutes of walking that beats 10,000 steps
idea.why_trending: Fitness creators are testing it this week and posting results.

script.title: The Walking Trick Beating 10,000 Steps
scenes: It's called interval walking, and it comes from research in Japan.
Walk fast for three minutes, then slow for three.
Repeat five times. That's just thirty minutes.
Studies linked it to better fitness and blood pressure than steady walking.
script.cta: Try it tomorrow and tell me how it went.

idea.hook_angle: Why brown noise quiets a busy brain
idea.why_trending: Study-with-me streams switching from white to brown noise.

script.title: Why Brown Noise Helps You Focus
script.hook: White noise is out. Brown noise is in.
scenes: Brown noise is deeper, like a waterfall or heavy rain.
It puts more energy in low frequencies, so it feels softer.
That steady rumble masks sudden sounds that break concentration.
Science is still early, but lots of people swear by it.
script.cta: Save this for your next study session.
script.description: The difference between white and brown noise, fast.

idea.hook_angle: Square windows once tore planes apart
idea.why_trending: TIL post with 40k upvotes in the last 6 hours.

script.title: Why Plane Windows Are Never Square
script.hook: Square windows used to rip planes apart.
scenes: In the 1950s, early jetliners had square windows.
Corners concentrate stress every time the cabin pressurizes.
Over many flights, cracks grew from those corners.
Round windows spread the stress evenly, so they stay strong.
script.description: The engineering lesson behind round airplane windows.

idea.why_trending: Office workers posting afternoon slump hacks.

script.title: The Coffee Nap Actually Works
script.hook: Drink coffee, then take a nap.
scenes: Caffeine takes about twenty minutes to kick in.
A short nap clears adenosine, the chemical that makes you sleepy.
Wake up just as the caffeine lands.
Keep it under twenty minutes so you don't wake up groggy.
script.cta: Tag the friend who needs this at 3pm.

idea.hook_angle: Octopuses might be dreaming in color
idea.why_trending: Aquarium clip resurfaced and is going viral again.

script.title: Do Octopuses Dream?
scenes: Octopuses have two kinds of sleep, quiet and active.
During active sleep, their skin flashes through colors.
The patterns look like what they show when hunting or hiding.
Scientists think it could be a replay of their day.

idea.hook_angle: A month of rain in one hour
idea.why_trending: Monsoon cloudburst news trending in India.

script.title: A Month of Rain in an Hour
script.hook: A month of rain, in one hour.
scenes: That's a cloudburst: extreme rain over a small area.
Warm, wet air gets pushed up mountains fast.
It cools, condenses, and dumps everything at once.
Hills funnel the water, which is why floods hit so fast.
script.cta: Share this so people know the warning signs.

script.title: 3 Desk Upgrades Under $30
script.hook: Three cheap fixes for a messy desk.

Clear surface, warm light, a bit of green. Done.

title: Northern lights seen unusually far south

idea.hook_angle: Your phone sees the aurora better than you do
idea.why_trending: Geomagnetic storm alerts and photo posts tonight.

script.title: Why Your Phone Sees the Aurora
script.hook: Your phone sees colors your eyes miss.
scenes: The sun just threw a burst of particles at Earth.
They hit our atmosphere and make the air glow.
In the dark, your eyes barely detect color.
Long-exposure cameras catch the reds and greens you can't see.
script.cta: Go outside tonight and point your camera north.
script.description: Why phone cameras capture the aurora better than eyes.

script.title: Never Waste Sourdough Discard
script.hook: Stop throwing your starter in the bin.
scenes: Spread your discard thin on a baking tray.
Brush with olive oil and sprinkle salt and herbs.
Bake low and slow until it's crisp.
Snap into crackers. Zero waste, real flavor.
script.cta: Save this for your next feeding day.

idea.why_trending: Debate thread exploded after a viral kitchen video.

script.title: The Five-Second Rule Is a Lie
scenes: Researchers dropped food on different floors and timed it.
Bacteria transferred in under one second.
Wet food picked up the most; dry food much less.
Carpet transferred less than tile. Surprising, right?
script.cta: Would you still eat it? Comment below.
script.description: What science says about the five-second rule.

idea.hook_angle: The order you add things changes everything
idea.why_trending: Monsoon weekend; chai recipe reels spiking.

script.title: Make Chai the Right Way
script.hook: You're making chai in the wrong order.
scenes: Boil water with crushed ginger and cardamom first.
Add tea leaves and let them go dark.
Now add milk and bring it up twice.
Sugar last, strain, and pour it high.
script.description: The order that makes chai taste better.
